timing.note: only 1 fully-covered eclipse(s) in the data - at least 3 are needed to test the period for timing changes

writeup: TIC 313590380 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 12.4409 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.07%, with a detection signal-to-noise ratio of 11.3. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis shows a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 6.3, but the centroid offset of 12.3 arcsec from the target raises an important question: TESS's resolution cannot confidently separate this star from a nearby bright neighbor. The centroid measurement falls within the pipeline's stated systematic uncertainty, making it unclear whether the dimming truly originates from the intended target or from the companion star instead. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs checked.
